title: Cross-consecration in the Roman Pontifical asks Christ’s true Cross to sanctify a stone/metal cross so its ‘merit’ frees souls—against Trent’s ‘no virtue in images’
source_text: XXVI. Praeterea Concilium Tridentinum statuit non esse credendum, imaginibus inesse virtutem aliquam, propter quam sint colendae. Sed contrarium supponit Ecclesiae Romanae praxis, non tantum in illa modo descripta oratione, in qua imagini vultus Christi tribuitur vis per quam lumen fundat cordibus, sed in aliis etiam, quae in Ecclesia illa sunt magis solennes atque usitatae. Nam cum Episcopus benedicit crucem ex lapide, vel metallo, ad Christum Dominum nostrum orationem habet, quae Pontificali Romano inserta est, titulo de benedictione novae crucis. In qua oratione opponens veram crucem cui Christus affixus est, cruci isti ex metallo vel lapide, A Christo Domino petit, ut crucem illam consecrandam, verae suae crucis sanctitate sanctificet, ac praestet ut merito crucis istius lapideae, vel argenteae, animae famulorum Christi omni careant perpetrato peccato. Orationis verba sunt, Nullum tibi debitum amplius munus est, quam quod tibi tunc corporis dedicavit affixio, nec tibi est magis familiaris oblatio, quam quae familiari manuum tuarum extensione sacrata est. Illis ergo manibus hanc crucem accipe, quibus illam amplexus es; & de sanctitate illius hanc sanctifica; & sicuti per illam mundus expiatus est a reatu, ita offerentium famulorum tuorum animae devotissimae hujus crucis merito, omni careant perpetrato peccato.
pass_a_gloss: Besides, the Council of Trent decreed that it is not to be believed that any virtue inheres in images because of which they should be cultivated. But the practice of the Roman Church assumes the contrary, not only in that prayer just described, in which power to pour light into hearts is attributed to the image of Christ’s face, but also in others which in that Church are more solemn and customary. For when a Bishop blesses a cross of stone or metal, he has a prayer to Christ our Lord inserted in the Roman Pontifical under the title of the blessing of a new cross. In which prayer, opposing the true cross to which Christ was affixed to that cross of metal or stone, he asks of Christ the Lord that He would sanctify that cross to be consecrated with the holiness of His true cross, and would grant that by the merit of that stone or silver cross the souls of Christ’s servants may be free from every committed sin…
pass_b_english: Trent denies inherent virtue in images; yet Pontifical cross-blessing asks Christ to load a new stone/metal cross with true-Cross holiness so its ‘merit’ cleanses souls—and the Veronica prayer already ascribed light-giving power to an image.
